cleared.check: geth v1.17.10 interpreter structure in the release binary: which code an untraced call or block import runs.
cleared.result: Untraced execution runs (*EVM).execUntraced (interpreter_gen.go:18, 21,088 bytes on amd64). Because the release is built with a PGO profile, the bodies of ADD, MUL, SUB, DIV, MULMOD, SIGNEXTEND, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO, AND, OR, NOT, SHL, SHR, SAR, the PUSH and DUP and SWAP cases, JUMP and JUMPI are inlined into that one function and are different machine code from the out-of-line op functions; MUL, DIV, MULMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SLT, SGT, SHL, SHR and SAR still call holiman/uint256 routines, and validJumpdest is called. SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, EXP, BYTE and the rest go through the per-fork table to the out-of-line handlers. Earlier cycles ran only the out-of-line handlers of geth-family builds, so the inlined copies had never run from a binary.

cleared.check: Task 2, reth v2.11.0 x86_64: the 25 arithmetic, comparison, bitwise and shift handlers of both handler families of the binary's instruction tables, with every function they reach.
cleared.result: The R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocations hold 26 instruction tables in two families (X 0x7f2fdd0..0x7f35dd0, Y 0x7f375d0..0x7f3d5d0); within a family every fork table points these opcodes at one handler, or at the undefined handler before the opcode existed. Handler ABI read from ADD: rdi packs pc<<11 with the stack length, rsi the stack, rdx the gas, status byte at context+0x147. Both families give the Python word on 1,137,754 cases (8 files, battery, targeted, v4shapes, c27, ruint121, provevec, pow2, random), 0 mismatches, 0 model errors, 271,445,048 emulated instructions, with the pc and stack length checked after every call.

cleared.check: Task 3: jump destination analysis of each binary on the PoolManager runtime (research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json, 24,009 bytes), cuts inside its last PUSH instructions, programs that end inside PUSH1..PUSH32 and random programs, and where the analysis is cached.
cleared.result: geth amd64 and arm64 (codeBitmapInternal and (*Contract).validJumpdest with Code at +0x50 and analysis at +0x38): 1399 programs each, no bitmap or destination mismatch; on the PoolManager the model accepts 610 destinations and rejects the 29 JUMPDEST bytes inside push data, and all 418 pushed jump targets are valid. erigon amd64: both kernels the binary can select, codeBitmapSSE4 (its assembly routine jumpdestBitmapSSE4 for 32-byte steps plus the inlined tail) and codeBitmapGeneric, on 1528 program runs, then validJumpdest on 1,971,918 destinations: no mismatch, 610 marked and 29 rejected on the PoolManager by both. reth amd64: the AVX-512 VBMI kernel, the AVX2 kernel (the baseline of this x86-64-v3 build, so no SSE4.1 kernel exists) and the scalar tail, 23253, 23253 and 23253 programs, 0 mismatches, 0 errors, every instruction of the two vector kernels reached. Caches: geth keeps the bitmap in a layered map keyed by the 32-byte code hash (jumpdests.go), local per EVM and shared, and analyses code without a hash per Contract; erigon keeps it in jumpDestCache, a 64 MB LRU keyed by the code hash bytes and never unwound (contract.go jumpdestAnalysis); reth builds it lazily once per bytecode object (0x42cdb30 takes a once-cell), and its bytecode cache is keyed by code hash as cycle 34 read.

cleared.check: Task 6: what a difference would mean for an ordinary account.
cleared.result: No handler, loop, conversion or jump analysis run of the three release binaries differs from the specification, so no line of src/ computes or decides anything else on these builds, and there is nothing an ordinary account could gain or lock through them. If one client had differed, a block it built would be rejected by the other two, and its eth_call answers would differ from the chain the majority writes; this was not observed.
